messages.subject: User-defined probability densities
parts:
Hi,

I have recently updated to Stan 2.10 and am wanting to understand how to define a custom probability density. Up until now I had done the following (which works):

functions{
  ## Function that returns the log pdf of the wrapped-Cauchy
  real wrappedCauchy_log(real aPhi, real aRho, real aMu) {
    return(- log(2*3.14159265) + log(1-aRho^2) - log(1+aRho^2-2*aRho*cos(aPhi-aMu)));
  }
}

model {
    for (i in 1:K}
        increment_log_prob(wrappedCauchy_log(phi[i],rho,mu));
    }
}

Here `phi' is the variable, and 'rho' and 'mu' are parameters. The function `rwrappedCauchy_log' returns the log pdf for the wrapped Cauchy distribution.

I get some warnings with the above on Stan 2.10 about replacing `_log' with `l_pdf'. I have had a look in the manual (section 19.5 on `User-defined probability functions') and it seems that I can do something more 'Stan-native' by doing something like:

phi[i] ~ wrappedCauchy(rho,mu);

Although the above doesn't seem to work... Is there a way to do this? If so, how should I do this?

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] User-defined probability densities
parts:
You should be able to define

wrappedCauchy_lpdf

and use

y ~ wrappedCauchy(...);

if all the types match. pi() is built in,
and we have log1m() and log1p() functions which
are more stable than what you're writing here.

We haven't had this new version out long, so if you
have problems, please send us the whole model file
and the whole output error you get.

- Bob
